Critical Throw.description: Upon reaching 5th level, the master thrower receives the Improved Critical feat applicable to any thrown weapon for which she possesses Weapon Focus.

Deadeye Shot.description: When employing this technique, the critical multiplier of a chosen thrown weapon type rises by one increment (for instance, a hand axe would critically multiply damage by 4 rather than the usual 3). This bonus cannot be combined with any other effect that raises critical multipliers.

Defensive Throw.description: Before making a thrown weapon attack while standing in a threatened area, a master thrower with this technique can attempt a Concentration check (DC 10 + the number of enemies threatening her). On a success, her thrown weapon attacks do not provoke attacks of opportunity for the remainder of that round. On a failure, enemies may take attacks of opportunity against her as usual.

Doubletoss.description: Using a standard action, a master thrower with this technique can hurl two weapons simultaneously at one or two targets that are each within 30 feet. She may add her full Strength modifier to the damage of both weapons, rather than applying only half her Strength bonus to the off-hand weapon. Standard two-weapon fighting penalties still apply.

Evasion.description: Starting at 2nd level, the master thrower gains evasion. When she succeeds on a Reflex save against an effect that would normally deal half damage on a successful save, she takes no damage instead. This ability only functions while wearing light armor or no armor, and is unavailable when she is helpless (for example, unconscious or paralyzed). If the character already possesses evasion, she instead gains improved evasion, which works identically except that a failed Reflex save results in only half damage rather than full damage.

Palm Throw.description: When wielding small thrown weapons such as darts, shuriken, or daggers (other weapons may qualify at the GM's discretion), a master thrower with this technique can launch two of the chosen weapon using a single attack roll. Damage is determined independently for each weapon, but the character's Strength modifier is not added to either damage roll.

Quick Draw.description: At 1st level, the master thrower receives the Quick Draw feat as a bonus.

Snatch Arrows.description: At 4th level, the master thrower gains the benefits of the Snatch Arrows feat, regardless of whether she meets its normal prerequisites.

Sneaky Shot.description: Immediately before executing a ranged attack, a master thrower with this technique may spend a move action to make a Sleight of Hand check contested by the target's Spot check. If the master thrower prevails, the target loses its Dexterity bonus to AC against that attack.

Thrown Weapon Trick.description: At 1st level and again at every second level after that, the master thrower selects one thrown weapon trick from the available options. Each selection is permanent and cannot be swapped out later. No trick may be chosen more than once. Every trick applies only when using a thrown weapon for which the character has Weapon Focus.

Trip Shot.description: A master thrower with this technique can attempt to trip a distant opponent (beyond 5 feet) using a thrown weapon. She makes a standard ranged attack with the thrown weapon; if it hits, it deals damage normally and she then makes a Dexterity check with a +4 bonus opposed by the target's Dexterity or Strength check (using whichever ability has the higher modifier). Additional modifiers may apply to this opposed check. If the master thrower wins, the target is knocked prone. This benefit does not stack with the Improved Trip feat.

Tumbling Toss.description: While wearing light, medium, or no armor, a master thrower with this technique can throw a single weapon at any point during an acrobatic tumble as a standard action. If her Tumble check result is 25 or higher, this ranged attack does not provoke attacks of opportunity, regardless of how many foes threaten her.

Two with One Blow.description: When attacking two opponents who are standing adjacent to one another, a master thrower with this technique may accept a -4 penalty on the attack roll to attempt hitting both targets with a single thrown weapon. Depending on the roll and each target's Armor Class, the attack might strike one, both, or neither opponent. Damage is calculated separately for each target. If the roll threatens a critical hit, confirmation rolls are made individually for each target.

Weak Spot.description: This technique is available only to master throwers who have reached 5th level. When throwing a weapon at a creature of her own size category or larger, the character may make a ranged touch attack in place of a standard attack roll. On a successful hit, her Strength bonus does not apply to the damage dealt.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency.description: This prestige class does not grant proficiency with any weapons or armor.
